title: Cell potential under nonstandard conditions (AP); Quantitative electrolysis (Faraday)
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AP Chemistry (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: RX10#t3 term and clue written for the game; RX08#t2 term and clue written for the game; RX08#t3 term and clue written for the game; RX10#t1 term and clue written for the game. Questions: RX08#N.3, RX10#N.3, RX08#N.6, RX10#N.6, RX08#N.7, RX10#N.10, RX08#N.8, RX08#N.9.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Standard conditions
items.clue: Every solute at 1 M and every gas at 1 atm, so that Q = 1.

items.label: Current
items.clue: Measured in amperes: the number of coulombs passing per second.

items.label: Charge
items.clue: Found from I × t with the time in seconds; measured in coulombs.

items.label: Nernst equation
items.clue: The relation E = E° − (RT/nF) ln Q, showing that E falls as Q rises.

questions.stem: A steel spoon is nickel-plated, using a nickel anode in NiSO₄(aq). Which pair of half-equations is correct?

options.text: Cathode: Ni(s) → Ni²⁺(aq) + 2e⁻. Anode: Ni²⁺(aq) + 2e⁻ → Ni(s).
Cathode: Ni²⁺(aq) + 2e⁻ → Ni(s). Anode: Ni(s) → Ni²⁺(aq) + 2e⁻.

questions.explanation: Nickel is deposited on the spoon (cathode) and the nickel anode dissolves. 2 electrons gained, 2 lost.

questions.stem: A galvanic cell based on the reaction Zn(s) + Cu²⁺(aq) → Zn²⁺(aq) + Cu(s) is connected to a light bulb and allowed to operate at constant temperature. How does the cell potential change as the cell operates, and why?

options.text: It decreases, because Q rises as Zn²⁺ forms and Cu²⁺ is used up, nearing equilibrium
It stays the same, because the potential is fixed by the two half-reactions in the cell
It decreases, because the zinc electrode becomes smaller as zinc atoms are oxidized
It stays the same until the Cu²⁺ ions are used up, and it then falls to zero

questions.stem: A student electroplates zinc onto a cathode from ZnSO₄(aq). During the experiment the mass of the cathode increases by 0.327 g. What quantity of charge passed through the cell? (F = 96,485 C/mol e⁻.)

A galvanic cell based on Zn(s) + Cu²⁺(aq) → Zn²⁺(aq) + Cu(s) is operating at 25°C. Solid Cu(NO₃)₂ is dissolved in the copper half-cell, increasing [Cu²⁺], and the measured cell potential increases. Which explanation of the increase is correct?

options.text: The cell's equilibrium shifts toward products, as Le Châtelier's principle predicts
More ions are present in solution, so more charge carriers raise the potential
E° for the cell increases, because the reactant ion is now more concentrated
Q decreases, so the cell is farther from equilibrium, and its driving force is greater

questions.explanation: Q = [Zn²⁺]/[Cu²⁺] falls when [Cu²⁺] increases, moving the cell farther from equilibrium (Q = K). The cell potential measures this driving force, so it increases.

questions.stem: A student electroplates nickel onto a cathode from NiSO₄(aq), using a constant current of 2.50 A. For how long must the current pass to increase the mass of the cathode by 2.348 g? (F = 96,485 C/mol e⁻.)

A concentration cell is made from two silver electrodes. The left electrode dips into 0.0010 M AgNO₃(aq) and the right into 0.10 M AgNO₃(aq), with a salt bridge between them. The cell is connected to a small motor and left to run. Which statement is correct?

options.text: Electrons flow from right to left, and E stays constant until the silver ions on the right are used up.
Electrons flow from left to right, and E falls toward zero as the two concentrations become closer.
No electrons flow, because E° is zero when both electrodes are made of silver.
Electrons flow from left to right, and E rises as the cell runs, because Q increases.

questions.stem: A constant current deposits 0.010 mol of Ag(s) from a solution containing Ag⁺(aq) in 30 minutes. The same current is then passed through a solution containing Au³⁺(aq). How long does it take to deposit 0.010 mol of Au(s)?
questions.explanation: Au³⁺ gains 3 electrons, Ag⁺ gains 1. Three times the charge at the same current takes three times as long.

questions.stem: A spoon is silver-plated using a silver anode in AgNO₃(aq). A current of 0.150 A passes for 20.0 min. What mass of silver is lost from the anode? (F = 96,485 C/mol e⁻; Ag = 107.87 g/mol)

options.text: 0 g, because only the spoon changes mass
